source_details.f13: WITH THE HISTORIC MID-TERM TURNOUT AND THE NEWLY ESTABLISHED CONDITIONAL VOTING (SAME DAY REGISTRATION)- VOTERS IN OUR COUNTY DID EXPERIENCE LONG WAIT TIMES. VOTERS WISHING TO VOTE PROVISIONAL AT THE POLLS WERE ABLE TO VOTE WITH RELATIVE EASE AND NO EXTENDED WAIT TIMES. IN THE EARLY MORNING AND MID MORNING CONDITIONAL VOTING (SAME DAY) THE WAIT TIME WAS AROUND 25-30 MINUTES. NEAR 4:30PM UNTIL POLLS WERE CLOSED VOTERS WISHING TO VOTE BY CONDITIONAL BALLOT (SAME DAY) WAITED APPROXIMATELY ONE HOUR AND A HALF.
THIS SURVEY IS VERY LONG AND TIME CONSUMING.  IT PUTS A BOURDON ON SMALLER COUNTIES WITH VERY FEW STAFF MEMBERS AND MULTIPLE HATS (DUTIES/DEPARTMENTS).

source_details.f12comments: BAY COUNTY UTILIZED 6 MEGA VOTING SITES ACCESSIBLE TO ALL VOTERS. PRECINCT VOTING WAS NOT AN OPTION DUE TO HURRICANE MICHAEL.
source_details.f13: HURRICANE MICHAEL CAUSED LIMITED POLLING LOCATIONS AND FREQUENT POWER OUTAGES AT THE POLLING LOCATIONS. WE SET UP 6 MEGA VOTING SITES EQUIPPED WITH ELECTRONIC POLL BOOKS AND DIRECT PRINT BALLOTS. EXTRA ACCESSIBLE VOTING EQUIPMENT (EXPRESSVOTE UNITS) WERE USED AS BACK UPS WHEN THE ELECTRICITY WENT DOWN IN ORDER TO ALLOW POLLING LOCATIONS TO REMAIN OPEN AND FUNCTIONING WITHOUT INTERRUPTION.

source_details.f1comments: FLORIDA IS NOT AN ALL MAIL-BALLOT JURISDICTION
source_details.f13: THE SECTION C REQUIREMENT TO INCLUDE ALL FORMS OF IN-OFFICE VOTING IN THE CATEGORY OF EARLY VOTING HAS SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED THE LEVEL OF COMPLEXITY AND PREPARATION TIME NEEDED TO COMPLETE THE SURVEY. THE ONLY WAY THE COUNTY HAS TO IDENTIFY IN-OFFICE VOTERS IS TO RUN SPECIAL QUERIES OF THE VOTERS WHO PICKED UP THEIR BALLOTS AT AN OFFICE LOCATION BEFORE ELECTION DAY AND EXTRACT THEM FROM OTHER MAIL BALLOT REPORTS. BECAUSE WE HAVE NO WAY TO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN PICKUPS THAT WERE VOTED IN OFFICE AND THOSE THAT WERE TAKEN AND RETURNED BY MAIL, THESE DATA ARE OF QUESTIONABLE VALUE. FURTHER, THE REJECT DATA FOR THESE PICKUPS ARE NO LONGER CAPTURED IN SECTION C OR ELSEWHERE IN THE SURVEY. EACH COUNTY WILL HAVE ITS OWN INTERPRETATION AND METHODS FOR IDENTIFYING IN-OFFICE VOTERS AND REWORKING THE DATA THEY HAVE PREVIOUSLY COMPILED FOR TABULATION AND REPORTING OF MAIL BALLOT DATA. THE NEED FOR CUSTOM QUERIES AND ADDITIONAL MANIPULATION OF DATA MEANS WE CAN NO LONGER RELY SOLELY ON OUR VALIDATED REPORTS. THE INCREASED POTENTIAL FOR INACCURACIES AND LACK OF DATA UNIFORMITY POTENTIALLY COMPROMISES THE INTEGRITY OF SOME OF THE SURVEY DATA.    THE REJECTED BALLOT DATA REPORTED IN VARIOUS SECTIONS INCLUDE THE NUMBER OF BALLOTS RECEIVED AFTER THE ELECTION DEADLINE. TO ENSURE STANDARDIZATION OF THESE DATA, A TIME FRAME SHOULD BE SPECIFIED FOR COLLECTING INFORMATION ON LATE BALLOTS.

source_details.f12comments: ALL BALLOTS ARE SENT TO THE COURTHOUSE TO BE STORED UNTIL ELECTION DAY.  ELECTION DAY, THE INSPECTORS BRING THE VOTED BALLOTS TO THE COURTHOUSE AT THE END OF THE DAY.  EVERYTHING IS COUNTED AT THE COURTHOUSE UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE CLERK AND THE ELECTION BOARD

source_details.f13: BESIDES THE AGING OF POLL WORKERS, THE BIGGEST CHALLENGE IS THE DISTANCE THAT MANY OF THE VOTERS MUST TRAVEL TO THEIR POLLING PLACE, AS IN WESTERN NEBRASKA WE HAVE VOTERS LIVING QUITE A DISTANCE FROM TOWN, AND MANY OF THE ROADS ARE NOT GOOD IN CASE OF BAD WEATHER.  I WOULD VERY MUCH LIKE TO SEE "MAIL VOTING" FOR THOSE COUNTIES LIKE US THAT ARE JUST BARELY OVER THE 10,000 POPULATION LIMIT FOR MAIL IN VOTING.  NEIGHBORING COUNTIES, MORRILL, GARDEN AND DAWES ALL HAD SUCCESS WITH THEIR MAIL-IN VOTING.  THIS WAS THE FIRST YEAR WE HAVE HAD PROBLEMS WITH OUR 650, AND HAD TO FEED BALLOTS THROUGH ONE AT A TIME FOR ONE PRECINCT, (TOOK LONGER THAN USUAL, BUT I REMEMBER HAND COUNTING!!!!), BUT EVERYTHING ELSE WITH IT WORKED GOOD.  WE HAD A GOOD ELECTION AND I AM SO GRATEFUL FOR THE HELP FROM ES&S, SOS OFFICE AND MY STAFF.

source_details.f13: WE DID HAVE A COUPLE OF CASES OF VOTERS WHO CAME TO VOTE WHO WERE NOT LISTED IN THE ROSTER BOOKS BECAUSE THEY WERE IN THE SYSTEM AS A FELON, HOWEVER A CHECK AFTER THE ELECTION REVEALED THEY HAD BEEN CONVICTED OF A MISDEMEANOR, NOT A FELONY. THE VOTERS VOTED PROVISIONALLY, SO ALL WORKED OUT, BUT WE ARE FINDING DISCREPANCIES IN THE SYSTEM AS TO WHAT THEY ARE ARRESTED/CHARGED WITH VERSUS WHAT THEY ARE CONVICTED OF. IMPROVED COMMUNICATION WITH THE COURTS MAY HELP KEEP OUR VOTER RECORDS BETTER UPDATED. WE ALSO EXPERIENCED MORE PROBLEMS WITH THE U.S. POSTAL SERVICE THIS ELECTION. WE HAD MAIL THAT NEVER MADE IT TO VOTERS, BUT THEY CHECKED UP AND WERE ISSUED REPLACEMENT BALLOTS. WE HAD ONE REQUEST FOR A BALLOT THAT CAME IN AFTER THE ELECTION AND THE REQUEST LOOKED LIKE IT HAD BEEN SOAKED IN WATER. WE HAD MORE MAIL RETURNED TO US IN PLASTIC “WE’RE SORRY” BAGS FOR THIS ELECTION THAN IN THE PAST. ALSO DELIVERY TIME SEEMED TO TAKE LONGER. WE HAD LOCAL BALLOTS GO OUT THAT STILL HADN’T REACHED A VOTER AFTER 10 DAYS.

source_details.f13: STAFFING THE POLLS AND LONG LINES WERE OUR BIGGEST CHALLENGES. WHILE LINES CAN BE EXPECTED, IT IS OUR HOPE/WISH TO HAVE DOUBLE THE AMOUNT OF POLL WORKERS AT MANY PRECINCTS FOR THE NEXT ELECTION. IT WOULD HELP SPEED UP THE PROCESS. ONE OTHER AREA WE ARE ADDRESSING (REGARDING PRIMARY ELECTIONS) IS THE WAY BALLOTS ARE GIVEN OUT. WITH OPEN PRIMARIES, POLL WORKERS GET CONFUSED AS TO WHICH BALLOTS TO GIVE VOTERS.  WE HAVE DEVELOPED A NEW PLAN FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF NON-PARTISAN AND OPEN PRIMARY BALLOTS.

source_details.f13: THIS ELECTION WAS PROBABLY THE MOST CHALLENGING ELECTION IN MY 26+ YEARS IN CONDUCTING ELECTIONS: 1.) FROM MAIN OFFICE STAFFING ISSUES DUE TO POTENTIAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST 2.) M650 CENTRAL TABULATORS TECHNICAL ISSUES THAT CAUSED US TO STOP TABULATING BALLOTS AT 3:00 A.M. (THE MORNING AFTER ELECTION) UNTIL A TECH FROM ES&S COULD COME AND CHECK THE M650, WE THEN COMPLETED TABULATING VOTES AT 11:18 A.M., NOVEMBER 7TH – THE LATEST I HAVE EVER COMPLETED THE INITIAL TABULATING OF VOTES PRIOR TO THIS ELECTION WAS 2:00 A.M. 3.) LARGEST NUMBER OF AUTOMATIC RECOUNTS DUE TO CLOSENESS OF CANDIDATE VOTES, THEN FOLLOWED BY BREAKING OF TIES, WITH ONE RACE HAVING A (17) WAY TIE WITH EACH VOTER RECEIVING (1) VOTE 4.) ONE OF THE LARGEST MID-TERM ELECTION TURN OUTS THAT SAUNDERS COUNTY HAS EVER HAD OF 64% (WHICH IS A GOOD THING)

source_details.f13: WE HAD SOME ISSUES WITH 2  WASHINGTON COUNTY RESIDENTS WHO ARE IN RUSSIA WHO WERE NOT ABLE TO APPLY FOR BALLOTS BY EMAIL WITH THE FPCA.  THE EMAILS WOULD NOT GO THROUGH.
